app.title: NanoCore Editor
app.subtitle: Unofficial online editor for the Livtra NanoCore mini multi-effect processor
app.noHardwareNotice: No NanoCore found — plug it in over USB (or pair Bluetooth) and it connects automatically. No hardware? Switch to the Simulator to build a patch offline.

connection.title: MIDI Connection
connection.pairingHint: USB and Bluetooth both work. For Bluetooth here, pair the NanoCore at the OS level first (on macOS: Audio MIDI Setup → MIDI Studio → Bluetooth) — toggle Bluetooth off/on on the device to wake its advertising, and make sure nothing else (e.g. the official phone app) already holds the connection. Once paired, it shows up below like any other port. (Or use the "Bluetooth" transport above to pair directly from this page instead.)
connection.bluetoothHint: Opens the browser's device picker (Chrome/Edge/Opera only, requires HTTPS or localhost) and connects directly to the NanoCore's Bluetooth MIDI service — no OS-level pairing needed. Toggle Bluetooth off/on on the device first if it doesn't show up, and make sure nothing else (e.g. the official phone app) already holds the connection. Already connected? Selecting this again won't re-prompt — use Disconnect below first to pick a different device.
connection.noOutputs: No MIDI outputs found. Connect your NanoCore via USB and refresh.
connection.noBluetoothOutput: Not connected yet — click the Bluetooth transport button above to open the device picker.
connection.connectHint: Pick the right device above, then Connect — this also reads back whatever patch is actually loaded on it. Nothing is sent to the device before you connect.
connection.connectedHint: Connected — every change here now goes straight to the device. Disconnect to stop sending without picking a different port.
connection.channelHint: Must match the NanoCore's own MIDI Channel setting (device channel 0 = Omni, any channel works).

routing.warning: FX2 is set to {{type}}, which reuses MOD's parameter CCs (68-73). Editing MOD parameters right now will actually change FX2's {{type}} instead.

preset.title: Preset Library
preset.sendToDeviceHint: Transmits every block's on/off, type and parameter CC for the current patch. Remember to save it on the device afterwards (long-press MASTER) if you want it to persist.
preset.empty: No saved presets yet. Build a patch and click "Save as new preset".
preset.recallHint: Program Change only tells the NanoCore which of its own stored presets to load — it does not read the resulting parameters back into this editor.
preset.recallOffsetHint: Confirmed on hardware: the device's own preset display is 1 higher than the number here — sending 0 recalls what the device shows as preset "1", sending 5 recalls "6", and so on.
preset.renameHint: Renames the device's currently active/edited patch (live, like any other tweak — up to 8 characters, the device's real limit). This does NOT persist on its own: use Save to device slot below afterward, or it's lost on the next preset change.
preset.saveHint: Saves whatever the device currently has loaded (recalled preset plus any live tweaks) into a slot — it does NOT first push this editor's own patch to the device. Send the patch first if you want to save what you see here. Same 0-indexed / +1-on-the-device numbering as recall above.
preset.saveFailed: No response from the device — save may not have happened.

tuner.title: Tuner
tuner.note: Sends CC80 (0 = off, 127 = on) to remotely open/close the on-device tuner. The reference pitch (default 440Hz) is only adjustable on the device itself — no CC is documented for it.

global.title: Global Settings
global.hint: Not connected — this is a local-only reference, nothing here is transmitted until you connect. Once connected, these become live device controls.
global.hintLive: Live — reflects and controls the device directly.

log.title: MIDI Activity
log.empty: Nothing sent yet. Move a control to see outgoing MIDI messages here.

chain.loadedPresetRename: Rename this patch on the device (max 8 characters)

info.title: About the NanoCore
info.hint: Reference material from Livtra's own documentation — nothing on this page is editable or transmitted, it's here so you don't have to dig through the PDF.
info.bluetoothIntro: The NanoCore has a fully independent dual-mode Bluetooth module. Both modes can be turned on or off independently without interfering with each other.
info.bluetoothNote: The NanoCore MIDI module stays hidden until first paired from within the official mobile app; it only appears in your phone's Bluetooth settings after that initial pairing succeeds.
info.usbAudioText: The device is a driver-free class-compliant USB audio interface — connect it to a computer and it shows up automatically as "Nanocore". It also supports direct connection to phones/tablets via USB OTG for high-quality on-the-go recording and live streaming.
info.companionSoftwareText: Livtra also publishes a free official companion app for comprehensive device management: tone adjustment, preset import/export, NAM (Neural Amp Modeler) file import, third-party IR loading, and factory reset.

bluetoothMode.NanoCore Audio (BT Audio): Receives media audio from a phone or tablet. Once connected, your phone's music can be used as a backing track routed into the effects processor.
bluetoothMode.NanoCore MIDI (Wireless MIDI): Connects to the official mobile app for bidirectional parameter sync, control and editing — the wireless counterpart to this editor.
